about.title: About Student Loan Calculator - Education Debt Planning Tool
about.description: The Student Loan Calculator is a comprehensive education financing tool designed to help students and graduates calculate monthly payments, total costs, and repayment strategies for student loans. This calculator supports federal and private student loans, various repayment plans, and loan forgiveness scenarios. Whether you're planning for college costs or managing existing student debt, this tool provides accurate projections for education loan scenarios.

faq.q: What's the difference between federal and private student loans?
faq.a: Federal loans offer fixed rates, income-driven repayment plans, deferment options, and potential loan forgiveness. Private loans may have variable rates, fewer repayment options, but sometimes lower rates for qualified borrowers.

faq.q: What are current federal student loan interest rates?
faq.a: For 2023-24, federal undergraduate loan rates are 5.50% for direct subsidized and unsubsidized loans. Graduate student rates are 7.05%, and PLUS loan rates are 8.05%. Rates are set annually by Congress.

Income-driven repayment can lower monthly payments based on income and family size, but may increase total interest paid. It's beneficial if you have high debt relative to income or qualify for loan forgiveness programs.

faq.q: How much student debt is too much?
faq.a: A common guideline is to borrow no more than your expected first-year salary after graduation. Keep total monthly student loan payments under 10-15% of your gross monthly income for manageable debt levels.
